Bayesian spatially varying coefficients generalized linear model

Source: R/svcGLMexact.R
svcGLMexact.Rd

Fits a Bayesian generalized linear model with spatially varying coefficients under fixed values of the spatial process parameters and some auxiliary model parameters. The output contains posterior samples of the fixed effects, the spatially varying coefficients and, if required, finds leave-one-out predictive densities.

Usage

svcGLMexact(
  formula,
  data = parent.frame(),
  family,
  coords,
  cor.fn,
  process.type,
  spParams,
  priors,
  boundary = 0.5,
  n.samples,
  loopd = FALSE,
  loopd.method = "exact",
  CV.K = 10,
  loopd.nMC = 500,
  verbose = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

formula

a symbolic description of the regression model to be fit. Variables in parenthesis are assigned spatially varying coefficients. See examples.

data

an optional data frame containing the variables in the model. If not found in data, the variables are taken from environment(formula), typically the environment from which svcGLMexact is called.

family

Specifies the distribution of the response as a member of the exponential family. Supported options are 'poisson', 'binomial' and 'binary'.

coords

an \(n \times 2\) matrix of the observation coordinates in \(\mathbb{R}^2\) (e.g., easting and northing).

cor.fn

a quoted keyword that specifies the correlation function used to model the spatial dependence structure among the observations. Supported covariance model key words are: 'exponential' and 'matern'.

process.type

a quoted keyword specifying the model for the spatial processes: 'independent', 'independent.shared' or 'multivariate'. See details.

spParams

fixed values of the spatial process parameters, a list with tags phi (spatial decay) and, if cor.fn = 'matern', nu (smoothness). If process.type = 'independent', each is a vector of length \(r\), otherwise a scalar.

priors

(optional) a list with each tag corresponding to a hyperparameter name and containing hyperprior details. Valid tags include V.beta, nu.beta, nu.z, sigmaSq.xi and IW.scale. Values of nu.beta and nu.z must be at least 2.1. If not supplied, uses defaults.

boundary

Specifies the boundary adjustment parameter. Must be a real number between 0 and 1. Default is 0.5.

n.samples

number of posterior samples to be generated.

loopd

logical. If loopd=TRUE, returns leave-one-out predictive densities, using method as given by loopd.method. Default is FALSE.

loopd.method

character. Ignored if loopd=FALSE. If loopd=TRUE, valid inputs are 'exact', 'CV'. The option 'exact' corresponds to exact leave-one-out predictive densities which requires computation almost equivalent to fitting the model \(n\) times. The options 'CV' is faster as it implements \(K\)-fold cross validation to find approximate leave-one-out predictive densities (Vehtari et al. 2017).

CV.K

An integer between 10 and 20. Considered only if loopd.method='CV'. Default is 10 (as recommended in Vehtari et. al 2017).

loopd.nMC

Number of Monte Carlo samples to be used to evaluate leave-one-out predictive densities when loopd.method is set to either 'exact' or 'CV'.

verbose

logical. If verbose = TRUE, prints model description.

...

currently no additional argument.

Value

An object of class svcGLMexact, which is a list with the following tags -

priors

details of the priors used, containing the values of the boundary adjustment parameter (boundary), the variance parameter of the fine-scale variation term (sigmaSq.xi) and others.

samples

a list of length 3, containing posterior samples of fixed effects (beta), the spatially varying coefficients (z, an \(nr \times\) n.samples matrix whose rows \((j-1)n + 1, \ldots, jn\) correspond to the \(j\)-th varying coefficient) and the fine-scale variation term (xi).

loopd

If loopd=TRUE, contains leave-one-out predictive densities.

model.params

Values of the fixed parameters: phi and nu (NA for the exponential correlation function).

diagnostics

a list of diagnostics. Element numerical is a data frame with one row (one row per process, if process.type = 'independent') and columns min.pivot (the smallest relative Cholesky pivot of the \(n \times n\) spatial correlation matrix; values below 1e-8 indicate a nearly singular correlation matrix), min.cor and max.cor (the correlations of the two farthest-apart and of the two closest locations; values of min.cor above 0.95 suggest an effective range far exceeding the extent of the data, values of max.cor below 0.05 nearly uncorrelated locations). If verbose = TRUE, a "Diagnostics" section is printed when any threshold is crossed.

The return object might include additional data that can be used for subsequent prediction and/or model fit evaluation.

Details

With this function, we fit a Bayesian hierarchical spatially varying coefficients generalized linear model by sampling exactly from the joint posterior distribution utilizing the generalized conjugate multivariate distribution theory (Bradley and Clinch 2024). Suppose \(\chi = (s_1, \ldots, s_n)\) denotes the \(n\) spatial locations in \(\mathcal{S} \subset \mathbb{R}^2\) at which the response \(y\) is observed, with \(y(s)\) endowed with a probability law from the natural exponential family $$ y(s) \sim \mathrm{EF}(x(s)^\top \beta + \tilde{x}(s)^\top z(s); b(s), \psi) $$ for some positive parameter \(b(s) > 0\) and unit log partition function \(\psi\). Here, \(\tilde{x}(s)\) denotes the \(r\) covariates with spatially varying coefficients. The supported families ('poisson', 'binomial' and 'binary') and the hierarchical model are those of stvcGLMexact(), with $$ z_j \mid \sigma^2_{z_j} \sim N(0, \sigma^2_{z_j} R(\chi; \phi_j, \nu_j)), \quad \sigma^2_{z_j} \sim \mathrm{IG}(\nu_z/2, \nu_z/2), \quad j = 1, \ldots, r, $$ where \(R(\chi; \phi, \nu)\) is the exponential or Matern spatial correlation matrix with decay \(\phi\) and smoothness \(\nu\). If process.type = 'independent', each process has its own \((\phi_j, \nu_j)\); if process.type = 'independent.shared', they share one. If process.type = 'multivariate', \(z = (z_1, \ldots, z_r)\) is a multivariate Gaussian process with correlation matrix \(R(\chi; \phi, \nu)\) and an \(r \times r\) cross-covariance matrix with an inverse-Wishart prior. We fix the process parameters and the hyperparameters \(V_\beta\), \(\nu_\beta\), \(\nu_z\) and \(\sigma^2_\xi\); their defaults are as in stvcGLMexact().

References

Bradley JR, Clinch M (2024). "Generating Independent Replicates Directly from the Posterior Distribution for a Class of Spatial Hierarchical Models." Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics, 0(0), 1-17. doi:10.1080/10618600.2024.2365728 .

Pan S, Zhang L, Bradley JR, Banerjee S (2025). "Bayesian Inference for Spatial-temporal Non-Gaussian Data Using Predictive Stacking." Bayesian Analysis, In Press. doi:10.1214/25-BA1582 .

Vehtari A, Gelman A, Gabry J (2017). "Practical Bayesian Model Evaluation Using Leave-One-out Cross-Validation and WAIC." Statistics and Computing, 27(5), 1413-1432. ISSN 0960-3174. doi:10.1007/s11222-016-9696-4 .

Examples

data(simSpatial)
dat <- simSpatial[1:150, ]

mod1 <- svcGLMexact(y_svc_pois ~ x1 + x2 + (x1), data = dat,
                    family = "poisson",
                    coords = as.matrix(dat[, c("s1", "s2")]),
                    cor.fn = "matern", process.type = "independent",
                    spParams = list(phi = c(8, 4), nu = c(1.5, 1.5)),
                    n.samples = 100, verbose = FALSE)

# rows 1, ..., n of z hold the varying intercept, rows n+1, ..., 2n the
# varying slope of x1
n <- nrow(dat)
z_hat <- apply(mod1$samples$z, 1, median)
cor(z_hat[n + 1:n], dat$z_true)
#> [1] 0.8783756
